The clinical presentation — chronic, bilateral, symmetric, pruritic, scaly, crusted, slightly raised lesions on the upper arms for 5 months, without nail involvement, extra-lesional skin involvement, or systemic symptoms — raises concern for a chronic inflammatory or lymphoproliferative dermatosis. - **Mycosis fungoides (early patch/plaque stage)** — highest concern given chronicity, symmetry, histologic spongiosis *plus* need for IHC correlation;
